questions.question: Which artery provides the predominant blood supply to the femoral head?
questions.detail: The predominant blood supply to the femoral head is the medial femoral circumflex artery. Injury to its extra-osseous branches during trauma increases the risk of avascular necrosis.

questions.question: Which radiographic line represents the border of the posterior column of the acetabulum?
questions.detail: The ilioischial line represents the border of the posterior column, while the iliopectineal line represents the border of the anterior column.

questions.question: In an adult patient, an isolated fracture of the lesser trochanter should be considered which of the following until proven otherwise?
questions.detail: While lesser trochanter avulsions occur in athletic adolescents, in an adult, this specific fracture is highly suspicious for an underlying pathologic fracture.

questions.question: Why is a basicervical femoral fracture typically treated with internal fixation (ORIF) rather than arthroplasty, even if displaced?
choices: It is extracapsular and carries a lower risk of avascular necrosis.
It only occurs in young athletes.
The blood supply to the head is always preserved.
It is histologically a bone-forming tumor.
questions.detail: Basicervical fractures occur just distal to the joint capsule; being extracapsular, they have a lower risk of AVN and can be successfully treated with ORIF.

questions.question: Which statement regarding 'occult' hip fractures is correct?
choices: They are never seen on CT.
They occur in approximately 50% of trauma cases.
MRI is the gold standard for diagnosis with essentially 100% sensitivity.
Dual-energy CT is the only way to visualize them.
They only involve the greater trochanter.
questions.detail: Occult fractures are not evident on radiographs (present in up to 10% of negative films). MRI is the gold standard for diagnosis with nearly 100% sensitivity.

questions.question: A 'tip of the iceberg' fracture of the hip refers to a radiographic finding of a greater trochanter fracture that often masks an occult:
questions.detail: Greater trochanter fractures are often the 'tip of the iceberg,' as the true extent often involves an intertrochanteric fracture that is occult on radiography but evident on MRI.

questions.question: In a posterior hip dislocation, what is a characteristic radiographic finding?
choices: The femur is in external rotation.
The femoral head is displaced inferiorly.
The lesser trochanter is obscured due to internal rotation.
The femoral head appears larger than the contralateral side.
questions.detail: In posterior dislocations, the femur is typically in internal rotation and flexion, which rotates the lesser trochanter behind the medial femoral cortex, obscuring it.

questions.question: What is the most common pattern of femoral head migration in hip osteoarthritis (OA)?
questions.detail: Hip OA characteristically features superior-lateral cartilage space narrowing, leading to superolateral migration of the femoral head.

questions.question: A 'protrusio deformity' in a female patient is defined as medial deviation of the femoral head beyond the ilioischial line by more than:
questions.detail: Protrusio is defined as medial deviation >3 mm in males and >6 mm in females beyond the ilioischial line.

questions.question: Which condition is a common cause of axial (concentric) migration of the femoral head?
questions.detail: RA causes concentric acetabular cartilage loss, leading to axial migration, whereas OA more commonly causes superolateral migration.

questions.question: Cam-type femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is characterized by:
choices: An osseous convexity at the femoral head/neck junction.
Symmetrical narrowing of the SI joint.
questions.detail: Cam-type FAI features an osseous bump at the head/neck junction and is most common in young athletic males.

questions.question: An alpha angle of greater than how many degrees is considered abnormal when assessing for Cam-type FAI?
questions.detail: An alpha angle of >55 degrees is considered abnormal and defines the degree of the femoral osseous bump.

questions.question: The 'crossover sign' on a frontal radiograph is a classic indicator of which condition?
questions.detail: The crossover sign represents cranial acetabular retroversion, signifying overcoverage in pincer-type FAI.

questions.question: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is characterized by which of the following?
choices: A normal alpha angle on ultrasound.
questions.detail: DDH involves an abnormally shallow acetabulum and has an increased incidence in breech births, firstborns, and girls.

questions.question: What is the threshold for a normal alpha angle on a pediatric coronal hip ultrasound?
questions.detail: A normal alpha angle in pediatric hip ultrasound is greater than 60 degrees; an angle less than 60 suggests DDH.

questions.question: On a pediatric pelvic radiograph, the ossified femoral head should sit in which quadrant?
questions.detail: The femoral head should sit in the inner lower quadrant formed by the Hilgenreiner and Perkins lines.

questions.question: Septic hip arthritis in a child is considered an orthopedic emergency because it can lead to:
questions.detail: Rapid intervention is required in pediatric septic hip arthritis to prevent permanent joint destruction and growth arrest.

questions.question: Which radiographic finding, though insensitive, may suggest a hip effusion?
questions.detail: Widening of the space between the pelvic teardrop and the medial femoral head suggests the presence of a joint effusion.

questions.question: Early-stage Legg-Calvé-Perthes (LCP) disease typically demonstrates which finding on a Tc-99m MDP bone scan?
questions.detail: Early LCP shows a photopenic (cold) defect in the femoral epiphysis, whereas late LCP shows increased uptake due to repair.

questions.question: A radiographic clue for Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) is the lack of intersection of the femoral head by which line?
questions.detail: Klein's line is drawn along the lateral margin of the femoral neck; lack of intersection with the femoral head suggests SCFE.

questions.question: While Klein's line is drawn on the AP view, SCFE is often best evaluated on which projection?
questions.detail: Physeal widening and displacement in SCFE are best evaluated on the frog-leg lateral projection.

questions.question: Calcific tendinopathy about the hip most commonly involves which tendons?
questions.detail: The gluteus medius and rectus femoris tendons are common sites for globular calcific deposits about the hip.

questions.question: What is the typical volume of injectate administered for a diagnostic hip MR arthrogram?
questions.detail: A total intra-articular volume of 10–12 mL is typically used for diagnostic hip MR arthrography.

questions.question: The central depression in the femoral head that serves as the attachment site for the ligamentum teres is the:
questions.detail: The fovea capitis is the only area of the femoral head not covered by articular cartilage and serves as the attachment for the ligamentum teres.

questions.question: Which anatomical structure is not covered by cartilage and is located at the center of the acetabulum?
questions.detail: The pulvinar is located at the center of the acetabulum and is not covered by articular cartilage.
